mainTopic: How steady and complete use must be for a חזקה: exceptions, partners taking turns, unused patches of a field, and who must prove the years of use
overview: This amud keeps asking how complete and steady a person's use of a property must be to create a חזקה, a claim of ownership based on three years of use. First, the גמרא gives two exceptions. For traveling peddlers, בית דין raises the 'use was not steady' argument for them. A store in מחוזא, which is only used by day, needs only daytime use. Next comes a story: רמי בר חמא and רב עוקבא בר חמא took turns using a maidservant in alternate years. רבא rules that this turn-taking is not a חזקה, against each other or against an outsider, unless a written document made their partnership public. רבא then rules that someone who used a whole field except a small בית רובע acquires everything but that patch. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says an unplantable patch goes along with the rest of the field, but רב ביבי בר אביי objects that even rocky ground can be used for animals or for spreading produce. Finally, in a dispute over a house, רב נחמן tells the occupant to prove his years of use. רבא objects that the one taking property away must bring the proof, and the גמרא begins to show that each of them seems to contradict himself in another case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: מר זוטרא agrees the court argues on behalf of traveling peddlers
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא agrees that for peddlers who travel from town to town, בית דין raises the argument for them even if they do not raise it themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא agrees about peddlers who travel around the towns: even if the peddler did not make the argument, we, the court, make it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us about one case where מר זוטרא agrees that בית דין speaks up for a person who did not make an argument himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, according to מר זוטרא, an argument that the use of a property was not steady day and night only counts if the owner raises it himself. A traveling peddler is often away from home, and everyone knows it, so it is very likely others lived in his house without his knowledge. That is why בית דין raises the argument for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (here: agrees in this special case)
Peddlers, traveling salesmen
Who travel around from town to town
We make the argument for him

steps.confusionAlert: This is an exception for peddlers. It does not mean מר זוטרא changed his general view; for most people, the owner still has to make the argument himself.

phrases.english: And Mar Zutra agrees
regarding peddlers who travel around the towns,
that even though he did not make the claim,
phrases.notes: "He" is the peddler who owns the house. He didn't argue that the other person's use was not steady.

phrases.english: we make the claim for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits מר זוטרא's earlier position, which comes from the part of the daf before this section, by giving an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For traveling peddlers, בית דין raises the argument that the use was not steady, even if the peddler did not raise it.

steps.title: רב הונא agrees a store in מחוזא needs only daytime use
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא agrees that a store in מחוזא, which is only used during the day, does not need to be used at night to create a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא agrees about a store in מחוזא: it is used by day, and it is not used at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another exception: for a store that is normally only used in the daytime, daytime use alone is enough for a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual standard is steady use that matches how the place is normally used. Stores in מחוזא were normally closed at night, so nobody would use them at night anyway. Daytime use is therefore full use for this kind of property.

keyTerms.meaning: A store or shop
מחוזא, a busy trading town in Babylonia
By day
Night

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that what counts as steady use depends on how that kind of property is normally used.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna agrees
regarding a store in Mechoza –
which is used by day,
and is not used at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as Step 1 ("he agrees"), giving a second exception to the requirement of steady use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a store that is only used by day, daytime use for three years is enough to create a חזקה.

steps.title: Two brothers take turns using a maidservant, and someone challenges them
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא and רב עוקבא בר חמא bought a maidservant together and used her in alternate years. Then someone came and challenged their ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא and רב עוקבא בר חמא bought a maidservant together. One used her in the first, third and fifth years, and the other used her in the second, fourth and sixth years. Someone came forward and challenged their ownership of her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests the rule of steady use. This step sets up the case, and the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together the brothers used the maidservant for six straight years. But each brother alone never had three years in a row. When an outsider claims she is his, the question is whether their combined use counts as a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant
Together, jointly
Made use of
A person who challenges someone's ownership

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא וְרַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama and Rav Ukva bar Ḥama
bought a certain maidservant together.
One of them used her
phrases.notes: "מר... ומר" here just means "one... and the other."

phrases.english: in the first, third and fifth years,
and the other used her
in the second, fourth and sixth years.
A challenger came out against her,
phrases.notes: Someone showed up claiming the maidservant really belonged to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא וְרַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא זְבוּן הָהִיא אַמְּתָא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from general exceptions to a real case that tests whether broken-up use creates a חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: joint owners each used a maidservant in alternate years for six years, and an outsider challenged their ownership.

steps.title: רבא rules that taking turns breaks the claim against outsiders too
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the brothers took turns so that neither would gain a חזקה against the other. Since their use is not a חזקה between them, it is not a חזקה against anyone else either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבא. He said to them: Why did you do it this way? So that you would not gain a חזקה against each other. Just as it is not a חזקה regarding you, it is also not a חזקה regarding the rest of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא decides the case: the brothers' alternating use does not create a חזקה, so it does not protect them against the challenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asks a question and answers it himself: the brothers took turns on purpose, so that neither would ever have three years in a row against the other. Since neither brother has three straight years of use, their turn-taking does not count as a חזקה, and that holds against an outsider just as it does between the two of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim of ownership based on three years of steady use
You would gain a חזקה
Against each other
To the rest of the world, to anyone else

steps.whatToRemember: Use that is purposely split up between partners, so that neither has three years in a row, is not a חזקה. Not between the partners, and not against an outsider.
steps.confusionAlert: The two brothers are not fighting each other. The challenge comes from an outsider. רבא uses the brothers' own reason for taking turns to show why their use cannot protect them from him.

phrases.english: They came before Rava; he said to them:
Why did you act this way?
So that you would not gain a חזקה against each other;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּלְדִידְכוּ לָא הָוֵי חֲזָקָה,
phrases.english: just as for you it is not a חזקה,
for the rest of the world it is also not a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַאי טַעְמָא עָבְדִיתוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in Step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Alternating use between partners does not create a חזקה, either between the partners or against an outside claimant.

steps.title: A written partnership document makes it public
steps.stepSummary: רבא's ruling about the brothers applies only when the partnership was not written down. A written document spreads the word, so the partners can make a חזקה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when there was no document. But if a document was written, it makes the matter known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבא's ruling in Step 4. The ruling was that the brothers' turn-taking with the maidservant is not a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking turns normally doesn't show the world that both of them own her. But a written document creates 'קלא', public awareness that they are partners. So their shared use does count as a חזקה against outsiders.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We only said this when...': a phrase that limits an earlier ruling
A document or written deed
A 'voice': public awareness, word getting around

phrases.english: And we only said this
where no document was written,
phrases.notes: He means a document showing that the two brothers are partners sharing her use.

phrases.english: but if a document was written,
it has publicity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא כְּתוּב עִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's ruling in Step 4 to cases with no written partnership document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the partnership was written in a document, it is publicly known, and the partners' shared use makes a חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: A חזקה works through public awareness. A written document can supply that awareness even when the way the owners use the item doesn't.

steps.title: Using a field except for one small patch
steps.stepSummary: רבא: if someone used a whole field for the חזקה years except for a בית רובע, he acquires everything except that patch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he used all of the field except for a בית רובע, he acquires all of it except for that בית רובע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: how complete the use has to be to make a חזקה on a field. רבא gives a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה only covers the ground the person actually used. The small patch he never used isn't covered, even though it sits inside the same field.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'ate' it: he used the land and enjoyed its produce
A small area, big enough to sow a quarter-קב of seed
He acquired

phrases.english: רבא said:
If he used all of it (the field),
except for a בית רובע,
he acquired all of it, except for the בית רובע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲכָלָהּ כּוּלָּהּ, חוּץ מִבֵּית רוֹבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how complete the use of a field must be for a חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה covers only the parts of the field that were actually used.

steps.title: An unplantable patch goes along with the land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits רבא's ruling to a patch that can be planted. An unplantable patch is acquired together with the rest of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: We only said this when the patch can be planted. But if it can't be planted, he acquires it along with the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע adds a limit to רבא's ruling from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning: if the patch can't be planted, he had no normal way to use it. So leaving it alone doesn't break his חזקה, and it is acquired along with (אגב) the rest of the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for sowing, plantable
Along with the land, as part of the rest of the field

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּבַר זְרִיעָה הִיא,
phrases.english: We only said this where it (the patch) is fit for planting,
but if it is not fit for planting,
he acquires it along with the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּבַר זְרִיעָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's ruling from Step 6 to plantable patches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unplantable patch inside a field that was otherwise used is acquired along with the rest of the land.

steps.title: Even rocky ground can be used in other ways
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי objects: rocky ground also gets a חזקה, through keeping animals or spreading produce on it. So the unplantable patch should also need to be used that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי objected: If so, how would anyone acquire rocky ground? It must be by standing animals on it and spreading produce on it. Here too, he should have had to stand animals on the patch, or spread produce on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי challenges רב הונא's limit from Step 7. He points out that 'unplantable' doesn't mean 'unusable'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there is a way to make a חזקה on purely rocky land: use it for animals or for drying produce. So an unplantable patch can also be used that way. If he didn't do it, he hasn't made a חזקה on that patch.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it: introduces a challenge
'If that is so': introduces a problem that follows from the view just stated
Rocky ground
Animals
Produce, fruit

steps.confusionAlert: רב ביבי isn't saying rocky land can't be acquired. He's saying it is acquired through a different kind of use, so that use is required here too.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: רב ביבי bar אביי objected to this:
If so, rocky ground, by what would one acquire it?
Rather, by standing animals on it
and spreading produce on it;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְאוֹקוֹמֵי בָּהּ חֵיוָתָא,
phrases.english: here too, he should have stood animals on it,
or else spread produce on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, צוּנְמָא – בַּמֶּה יִקְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's limit from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's claim that an unplantable patch is acquired along with the rest of the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rocky land clearly can get a חזקה through non-planting uses. So an unplantable patch could have been used that way, and without such use there is no חזקה on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a חזקה depends on using the land in whatever way suits it, not only by planting it.
steps.whatToRemember: For a חזקה, each piece of land must be used in a way that fits it. Rocky or unplantable ground can be used for animals or for spreading produce.

steps.title: A dispute over who owns a house
steps.stepSummary: One man asks another why he is in his house. The occupant says he bought it and lived there for the years of חזקה. The original owner says he was living in faraway settlements.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to another: 'What are you doing in this house?' The other answered: 'I bought it from you, and I lived in it for the years of חזקה.' The first one said: 'I was away in the distant settlements.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new court case to set up a ruling. Two people argue over a house, and each gives his claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The occupant relies on the usual rule that living somewhere for the years of חזקה, together with a claim of purchase, proves ownership. The original owner does not answer the purchase claim directly. He only says he was far away. This sets up the question of who must prove what.

keyTerms.meaning: What do you want? Here it means 'What are you doing here?'
I bought it from you
I used it for the years of חזקה
Distant (literally 'inner') settlements, far away

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to another:
What are you doing in this house?
He said to him: I bought it from you,
and I used it for the years of חזקה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא בִּשְׁכוּנֵי גַּוּוֹאֵי הֲוַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I was in the distant settlements.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about חזקה claims in a house, separate from the field discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the occupant claims purchase plus the years of חזקה, and the original owner claims he was far away.

steps.title: רב נחמן: go prove that you lived there
steps.stepSummary: The case comes to רב נחמן, who tells the occupant to prove he really used the house for the years of חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רב נחמן. He said to the occupant: 'Go and prove your use of the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his ruling. The occupant has to bring proof, such as witnesses, that he really lived in the house for the full years of חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן puts the burden of proof on the person living in the house. Saying 'I lived here three years' is not enough. He must show it before his חזקה helps him.

keyTerms.meaning: Go clarify, meaning go prove
Your use (literally 'your eating') of the property

phrases.english: He came before רב נחמן,
He said to him: Go prove your use.
phrases.notes: 'Use' is literally 'eating.' It means living in the house or profiting from it for the years of חזקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the court's ruling on the case from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The occupant must prove that he really lived in the house for the years of חזקה.

steps.title: רבא objects: the one taking property away must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. The rule is that whoever wants to take something from another person must bring the proof, so the original owner should have to prove his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: 'Is this the law? The one who wants to take something away from his fellow must bring the proof!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling by quoting a basic rule about who carries the burden of proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The occupant is the one holding the house now. The original owner wants to take it from him, so according to רבא the original owner has to prove that the occupant did not live there. רב נחמן did the opposite and put the burden on the occupant.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this the law? (said as a challenge)
Whoever wants to take from another must bring the proof

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the 'מוציא', the one taking the house away, is the original owner, not the occupant, because the occupant is the one living there now.

phrases.english: רבא said to him: Is this the law?!
The one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the occupant must prove he used the house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The burden of proof is on whoever wants to take property from its holder. Here that is the original owner, not the occupant.

steps.title: Setting up contradictions in רבא's and רב נחמן's views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that רבא here seems to contradict himself, and so does רב נחמן. It begins a second story to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא points out a contradiction between this ruling of רבא and another ruling of רבא, and between this ruling of רב נחמן and another ruling of רב נחמן. For there was a certain man...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says each of the two אמוראים seems to hold the opposite position in another case, and it starts telling that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is explained yet. The other story begins with 'דְּהָהוּא' and continues on the next amud. In that story the positions of רבא and רב נחמן will seem to be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: And he points out a contradiction (literally 'throws' one against the other)
רבא's statement against another statement of רבא

phrases.english: And one points out a contradiction between רבא and רבא,
and a contradiction between רב נחמן and רב נחמן –
for there was a certain man

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the positions from steps 10 and 11 into the subject of a double contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבא's and רב נחמן's positions on the burden of proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another case will show each of them apparently holding the opposite view, which the next lines will lay out.
